title: Meta Unveils TextSeal2 to Improve Detection of AI-Generated Text

tickers.name: Meta Platforms, Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The company's latest method for tagging AI output embeds a hidden signal that allows detectors to flag generated text without introducing processing latency or limiting the variety of a model's answers. Detailed in a new research paper, the TextSeal2 system uses a technique called "copula mixing" to combine two secret keys into one virtual signal, ensuring every token sampled by the large language model carries a signature for later identification.

In benchmarks using a Qwen3.5-9B model, TextSeal2 identified 89% of 200-token responses at a 0.1% false-positive rate. This outperformed the original TextSeal and a rival tool, textGrain, which recorded detection rates of 71% and 67% respectively under the same conditions. Meta designed the tool to maintain effectiveness during speculative decoding, a speed-optimization technique that often degrades the signal used by other watermarking tools.

selectedTweets.text:
New Meta paper shows that blending 2 secret keys into 1 makes hidden watermarks in AI-written text easier to detect, even when the AI uses a common trick (like  speculative decoding) to write faster.

Watermarks hide a secret-key signal in which tokens an LLM samples, so a detector can later flag its text. Meta's earlier TextSeal picked 1 of 2 keys per token at random, so detection had to average both and lost signal.

TextSeal2 blends both keys into 1 virtual key plus fresh noise, so answers stay varied and every token carries full signal. For speculative decoding, it picks replacement tokens from the leftovers of the drafts' random races, so acceptance rates stay unchanged.

On Qwen3.5-9B with speculative decoding and equal diversity, it detected 89% of 200-token answers at a 0.1% false-positive rate. TextSeal caught 71% and textGrain 67%, at the same acceptance rate.
